subject: Re: Unexpected cross-tenant charges from staging keys — proposed reallocation & credit plan
messages:
From: Sana Malik <sana@mintedai.com>
To: Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Billing spike — possible staging key bleed into production

Hi Connor,

We noticed a significant jump on our September invoice tied to embed/replay calls (tokens). Our finance team flagged ~1.2M tokens that look like they originated from our staging environment but were billed to our production tenant. We only have one active production API key and multiple sandbox keys that should be excluded.

Can you help explain:
- How staging/sandbox keys could be attributed to a production entity?
- Whether Redwood can reassign those tokens to our sandbox usage and issue a credit for the production invoice?

I attached a short sample of the timestamps and request IDs we pulled (minted_usage_slice_q3.csv). We need an answer before our accounting cut on Oct 1.

Thanks,
Sana Malik
Director of Engineering, MintedAI
Sana Malik | mintedai.com

---
Attachment: minted_usage_slice_q3.csv (CSV, 48KB)

From: Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Sana Malik <sana@mintedai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Billing spike — possible staging key bleed into production

Hi Sana — thanks for the heads up and the sample. I dug into telemetry and a few things stand out:

Short summary:
- We see a set of request_ids (same ones in your CSV) that passed through our gateway with the production tenant header but used API keys that were recently rotated from a staging pipeline.
- There was a brief rollback in the key-namespace replication job on 2026-09-23 02:10 UTC that can cause a transient mapping mismatch (staging keys mapped to the wrong tenant tag).
- Impact window: ~2026-09-23 01:58 UTC to 2026-09-23 03:05 UTC. Estimated billed tokens in that window for your account: ~1.15M tokens.

Next steps I propose (so we move quickly before your billing cutoff):
1) Provisional reallocation: we can reclassify the tokens to your sandbox tenant for invoicing purposes and issue a provisional credit on the Sep invoice.
2) Root-cause remediation: ops will patch the replication job and add an immediate guard that prevents tenant header overrides during replay.
3) Evidence package: we will provide raw request traces (redacted), the job run logs, and a CSV with the before/after attribution.

Ben and Kimberly — looping you in to review the credit amount range and sign off on the provisional reallocation. Sana — if you can confirm the sample covers the same request IDs you see, I'll kick off the internal ticket and get the trace package ready.

—Connor
Connor Obrien
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

---
Attachment: (none)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: Billing spike — proposed reallocation & credit plan

Connor — forwarding my quick internal note.

We reviewed the telemetry and agree provisional reallocation is reasonable given the replication rollback window you identified. Notes for Finance/Revenue ops:
- Estimated credit band for Sep invoice: $2,700 - $3,100 (based on token unit price in the signed MPA and your usage tier).
- Ask: issue a provisional credit hold so MintedAI's Accounts Payable can close the period; finalize after evidence packet completes.
- Legal: no contract change needed; this is a one-off operational correction.

Kimberly — please prepare the evidence bundle (request traces with redactions, job logs) and the final credit calc so we can send a settlement confirmation to the customer.

Ben Carter
Sr. Billing Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

---
Attachment: proposed_credit_summary.xlsx (Excel, 12KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sana Malik <sana@mintedai.com>, Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Billing spike — proposed reallocation & credit plan

Hi Sana — thanks again for the sample. We've completed the evidence pack and final credit calculation.

What we did:
- Correlated your CSV request_ids with our raw traces and gateway logs.
- Verified the replication rollback window (2026-09-23 01:58–03:05 UTC) and confirmed the keys in question were in the staging keyset at time of calls.
- Reclassified 1,148,932 tokens from the production tenant to your sandbox tenant.

Resolution offered:
- Provisional invoice credit: $2,940 applied to the September invoice immediately (appears as \"Operational Adjustment - Sep 2026\").
- Finalization: we'll finalize accounting entries and send a reconciliation PDF after your team confirms the evidence bundle.
- Preventative measures: patch deployed to replication job; added an invariant check to block tenant-tag overrides during replay.

Evidence bundle and reconciliation link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xX-minted-usage-report (contains redacted traces, job logs, and the reconciliation CSV).

If Minted's accounting needs a vendor statement for their audit team, we can provide a one-page attestation summarizing the technical root cause and the remediation steps. Let me know and I'll prepare it.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Billing & Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
